top.title: Kyle Shanahan Rules Brock Purdy Out For Seahawks Clash
top.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images An ankle injury will cause San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy to miss Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan on Friday. Mac Jones takes over as the starter, with Kurtis Rourke serving as the backup, according to ESPN reporter Nick Wagoner. The team made this call after Purdy did not practice all week and his injury did not heal fast enough to allow him to suit up. During the second quarter of last week’s victory over the Minnesota Vikings, Purdy injured his left ankle. The injury happened when Purdy tried to escape defensive lineman Jalen Redmond and his foot bent awkwardly as he went to the ground. Shanahan knew about the issue at halftime but said it did not change how he called plays for the rest of that game. The coach ruled the injury out on Friday because it simply did not improve during the week. A Mid-Level Ankle Issue Shanahan explained the specific nature of the injury while speaking to reporters on Friday. “Anytime it’s not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse,” Shanahan said. He noted that the team had a feeling by Wednesday that Purdy would not be ready. “Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. [It] didn’t heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down,” the coach added. Purdy does not require surgery, and the expectation is that he will be ready for Week 13 versus the New York Giants. Shanahan remains optimistic about the timeline for his recovery. “It’s too soon [to tell] but I’m pretty optimistic about it,” Shanahan said. He acknowledged the sudden change in plans but expressed hope for the future. “But I was about this week to start and then it changes. So, hopefully it’ll be all right,” he told the press. Mac Jones Steps Up Again Jones is no stranger to this situation for the 49ers. In 2025, when Purdy suffered a turf toe injury, he started eight games in Purdy’s stead. During those contests, the 49ers went 5-3 with Jones posting a 62.7 QBR. He threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions in that span. This season, Jones has seen action only in mop-up duty, where he completed one pass on one attempt for 5 yards. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Left tackle Trent Williams voiced strong support for Jones after seeing his preparation this week. Williams highlighted the team’s confidence in him based on his past performance. “He was great last year when we needed him,” Williams said. The team expects Jones to handle the pressure of this big divisional game. “We expect him to be good this year,” Williams added. Shanahan praised Jones for his work during the week leading up to the matchup. “Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this with him last year, so everyone’s got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp, and he’s the same guy every day. It’s been a good week with Mac,” per ProFoo

top.title: INEC tests BVAS, result portal today
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. The list gives the state, local government area, ward, polling unit and delimitation code of each selected location. It runs alphabetically from Abia State to Zamfara State, with the FCT last. Abia has 368 entries, while Adamawa follows with 452. In the FCT, 124 polling units were selected across the six area councils. Abaji, Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali have 20 each, while the Municipal Area Council has 24. The exercise will simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. INEC said the value of the exercise lies in the faults it find

top.title: Iowa’s Hank Brown Proves CFP Dreams Are Real Again
top.description: Iowa Hawkeyes running back L.J. Phillips Jr. (21) carries the ball against Nebraska Cornhuskers linebacker Vincent Shavers Jr. (10) and Nebraska Cornhuskers defensive back Caleb Benning (28) Nov. 27, 2026 during a Big Ten football game at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. The No. 13 Hawkeyes crushed Nebraska 31-7 , marking their fifth straight victory. Brown scored three rushing touchdowns and added one passing touchdown. Iowa returns to contention for a Big Ten Championship Game berth and gains national attention thanks to this showing. The team now sits at 10-2 overall with a 7-2 record in the Big Ten conference. A loss would have ended their season, but this win keeps the door open for a national title run. While Brown shined with the ball, the Iowa defense shut the door on Nebraska completely. The unit allowed only five total touchdowns during this five-game winning streak. They held the Huskers scoreless in the second half for the third straight game in a row. Iowa leads the entire nation in scoring defense right now. The offense outgained Nebraska 329 yards to 260 yards, which was the first time a team has done so against Nebraska this season. Nebraska tried to fight back after winning against Ohio State the week before, but they could not stop the Hawkeyes. The Huskers recovered a muffed punt in the third quarter while trailing 10-7, yet they failed to score on that drive. After a third-down stop at the Iowa 35-yard line, they surrendered a score on the following drive. Jamal Rule rushed for 106 yards and scored a 21-yard touchdown for Nebraska in the second quarter. Despite his efforts, the Huskers fell to 7-5 overall and 4-5 in conference play. There are still specific combinations that must occur for Iowa to reach the Big Ten Championship Game. However, their path to the national playoffs remains clear if they keep winning. The Associated Press reported that the Hawkeyes have outscored their opponents 147-41 during this current winning streak. Brown opened the scoring with a 14-yard run in the first quarter. With 4:02 remaining, his 29-yard run ended the scoring. Against the Huskers, Iowa has claimed 11 victories in their last 12 matchups.

top.title: Death on the River: Some who came for rescue were more interested in stealing phones, bags, money — Survivor
top.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. top.title: 49ers-Seahawks roundtable: How much will who's under center matter?
top.description: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks passes the ball while being pressured by Romello Height #94 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter at Lumen Field on Oct. 11, 2026 in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) When the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Seattle to play the Seahawks seven weeks ago, it represented a big moment for both teams. The 49ers won, remaining undefeated, and have gone 4-1 since. After narrowly losing, the Seahawks have stumbled to 3-2. With Kyle Shanahan 's club riding high and leading the NFC but facing a game with Brock Purdy on the sidelines, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to these key questions going into Sunday's rematch. First, a general NFL question: the drama in Pittsburgh. Have we seen the last of Aaron Rodgers in uniform? Harrison Rich: It's often hard to side with Aaron Rodgers, but he seems to have the stronger argument here over Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. ESPN confirmed Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy , including sleeping in quarterback meetings and breaking down a halftime huddle by saying "1-2-3 Packers." Rodgers was waived Wednesday, but I'd imagine he plays football again in 2026 - assuming he wants to. He was still playing at a fairly high level and led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record before his ousting. Eric Branch: The constant in Aaron Rodgers' family and work drama: Aaron Rodgers. Given the late-career strife he's often been responsible for causing, it's notable that Rodgers' 22-season career began with him spending three good-soldier seasons sitting behind Brett Favre. Rodgers took a flamethrower to his long relationship with Mike McCarthy. It sounds as if much of what he alleged is true, but he broke an NFL code and left his playoff-contending teammates to deal with the fallout. Has he played his last snap? Not if an injury to a starting QB creates an urgent need. As former Cardinals GM Steve Keim once said of NFL teams rationalizing character concerns: "If Hannibal Lecter ran a 4.3, we'd probably diagnose it as an eating disorder." Ann Killion: I wouldn't be shocked if some playoff-bound team suffers an injury at quarterback and brings Rodgers in. I mean, who would be better? But, as the Black Friday broadcast team pointed out, Rodgers had already said this is his last year and has also emphasized that when he was done playing he will pull a "Keyser Soze" and disappear from public view. (Interesting to hear fellow former Cal Bear Tony Gonzalez put Rodgers on blast.) Yet there he was, airing his dirty laundry on the Pat McAfee show, blowtorching the coach he won a Super Bowl with, and texting Al Michaels during the Friday broadcast to further litigate his case. The guy desperately needs the spotlight. Pittsburgh crushed Denver, sending the message that they don't need Rodgers (though the players all still seem to like him). Rodgers' most amazing feat? Turning hapless McCarthy into a sympathetic character. Fred Warner

top.title: Nebraska Football Fails To Deliver With The Bright Lights Placed On The Program
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Rhule and Nebraska had an underwhelming performance in 31-7 loss to Iowa on Black Friday. Nebraska football has done enough to warrant Matt Rhule having another crack at things. But Black Friday was not one to remember for Husker Nation. Related: Iowa Earns Its Spot Inside The College Football Playoff Field Coming off quite possibly the biggest win in the coaching career of Rhule at Nebraska, the Huskers laid a massive egg. Iowa scored a 31-7 victory, continuing its domination in the series. Instead of riding the momentum generated by the win over Ohio State, the Huskers looked like the Nebraska of old. Uninspired. Iowa’s Offense Completely Dominated Nebraska It all started on the defensive side of the football for the Huskers. The Hawkeyes had over 300 yards of total offense, as Hank Brown ran in three touchdowns. Brown, who also had a passing strike for six, was efficient. He picked Nebraska’s secondary apart at will, continually finding open receivers in critical situations. The Hawkeyes ran for 156 yards as a team, led by 76 from L.J. Phillips, Jr. Related: Texas Tech Shows Incredible Grit, Toughness To Be College Football Playoff Contender And it wasn’t like Nebraska’s offense was struggling. They moved the ball, putting up 153 yards in the air and 107 on the ground. The explosive play was never really there. And Anthony Colandrea had an interception and was limited to minus-12 rushing yards. Huskers Have One More Chance To Gain Momentum This might be one of the biggest bowl games in Nebraska’s history in quite some time. The Huskers need momentum back on their side heading into the offseason. They are likely to be sent to a mid-level bowl game, such as the Cactus Bowl, Music City Bowl or Duke’s Mayo Bowl. top.description: Motorsport photo Toto Wolff has spent the past week sounding remarkably unfazed by Formula 1’s fiercest driver feud. George Russell , however, just hinted that Mercedes ’ team principal sounds rather different once the microphones are switched off. Speaking exclusively to Martin Brundle for Sky Sports F1 - in an interview previewed Friday ahead of its full broadcast before Sunday’s Qatar Grand Prix - Russell was pressed on Wolff’s diplomatic public stance toward Max Verstappen following their Las Vegas flashpoint. Russell stopped short of repeating private conversations, but left little doubt that Wolff’s off-camera assessment carries a sharper edge. "Well, I know where he [Wolff] stands off the record, so I won't probably repeat that," Russell said. "Toto and I were flying back after the race in Vegas, and we did have quite a laugh about the comments that were said after the race. But we just know how certain people go about their business." Why Wolff’s Las Vegas tone raised eyebrows That remark cuts straight into one of the paddock’s most scrutinised dynamics. Wolff’s public warmth toward Verstappen has been tracked closely ever since Mercedes pursued the Red Bull driver in 2025 - talks Russell himself confirmed to Sky Sports F1 in June 2025 had delayed his own contract renewal. Even after Wolff publicly shut down fresh rumours in March 2026 - insisting "The Max to Mercedes thing for now is not on" and backing Russell to stay with Brackley "until 2037" - photographs of Wolff and Verstappen holidaying together surfaced again in July 2026, keeping the speculation alive. Last weekend in Nevada put that dynamic back under the microscope. After final-practice contact at Turn 14 triggered public criticism from Russell, Verstappen answered by winning Saturday night’s Grand Prix while Russell clipped the barrier late while battling team-mate Kimi Antonelli and dropped to ninth. In the aftermath, Verstappen declared Russell "so far below my level" and took open satisfaction in his rival’s late error. Calling Verstappen "a deserving winner" who "made no mistakes" and "always had a response," Wolff brushed off the tension between the pair. top.title: Vero Beach football reaches state semifinals for second straight year
top.description: VERO BEACH — For the second consecutive year, Vero Beach football is headed back to the Florida state semifinals. The Fighting Indians defeated Edgewater 38-23 on Friday, Nov. 27 at Billy Livings Field at the Citrus Bowl to advance to the FHSAA Class 6A state semifinals. Vero Beach (12-1) will be making its first back-to-back state semifinal appearances since 1993-94. The Fighting Indians will learn their semifinal opponent after the conclusion of the remaining region finals. DeLand (11-1), which is ranked below Vero Beach in the latest MaxPreps state rankings, has already advanced to the Class 6A state semifinals. Vero Beach jumped all over Edgewater in the first half, building a 24-3 lead behind a touchdown pass from Makai White to Marcus Melbourne Jr. and touchdown runs by Jayden Lockhart and Marc Johns. The Fighting Indians piled up 269 total yards, including 200 on the ground, while limiting Edgewater to just 59. Lockhart added another rushing score early in the third quarter, ballooning Vero Beach's advantage to 31-3. Edgewater (8-5) battled back with a pair of touchdowns to cut the deficit to two scores, but Lockhart iced the game midway through the fourth quarter with his third rushing touchdown. top.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders throws a pass during the fourth quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Raiders 38-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns take on the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday. The Browns are a perfect 4-0 at home and coming off of a bye week. The Raiders have lost both starts with new quarterback Fernando Mendoza , but that also doesn’t mean they’re a pushover. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders: NFL.com (Various) Why Gennaro picked the Raiders: Will the third start be the charm for Fernando Mendoza? In his debut as Las Vegas’ QB1, the No. 1 overall pick sprinted out of the gates with 10 points in the first two drives vs. Seattle … but he appeared to run out of steam when the Raiders ran out of scripted plays. In his second go-around, Mendoza fell behind 17-0 in Denver before admirably rallying Vegas back to a seven-point, fourth-quarter deficit … but his late pick-six ultimately sealed the Raiders’ fate. top.title: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship
top.description: DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West played for its sixth PIAA District One football championship on Friday night. The Bucks won District One onfield titles under Mike Pettine in 1993 and 1997-99, as well as Mike Carey in 2000. Spring-Ford, like CB West, went into the game at War Memorial Field with identical 12-1 records. The Bucks finished the job, downing the Rams 34-0 behind a dominant rushing attack and suffocating defense. Senior Lou Cipollo ran for a pair of touchdowns while seniors Nick Miletto and Braylen Cope both scored a rushing touchdown. CB West will face the St. Joseph Prep/Nazareth winner in next weekend’s Class 6A semifinals. Prep led Nazareth 49-20 at the start of the fourth quarter. West had reached the district title game in 2022, when it lost at Garnet Valley, while Spring-Ford fell to Coatesville for the 2012 district championship. This is the Bucks' first district title in 26 seasons. Rob Rowan’s CB West squad defeated Perkiomen Valley 56-42, Central Bucks East 44-21 and Council Rock South 30-13 to reach the final, while Spring-Ford topped Quakertown 42-28, Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 and top-seeded Downingtown East 17-14 at districts. *Check back later tonight for much more on the game. What’s next for Spring-Ford Football? The season ended for the Rams. What’s next for Central Bucks West Football? The Bucks will face St. Joseph Prep or Nazareth in the state semifinals next weekend. top.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but it was enough to defeat the New York Rangers (13-11-1) 2-1 at the United Center on Friday. Andrew Mangiapane scored both of Chicago’s goals, his first two tallies of the season, Oliver Moore had two assists, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 31 shots as the Blackhawks extended their winning streak to four games. The Blackhawks are now 6-1-1 in eight games since an abysmal 0-3 Southeastern road trip earlier this month. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. nigeria.title: Death on the River: Some who came for rescue were more interested in stealing phones, bags, money — Survivor
nigeria.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. nigeria.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. nigeria.title: Meet Emmanuel Emegha, Chelsea’s new striking sensation who has Nigerian roots
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Chelsea’s latest attacking prospect, Emmanuel Emegha, is already giving supporters reasons to pay attention after scoring against Nottingham Forest on Friday. While the Blues trailed by two goals to nil, the 23-year-old striker, who joined Chelsea from French side Strasbourg, came off the bench to replace Danny Welbeck, found the net in the 54th and 89th minutes, and offered the Blues a lifeline in their Premier League encounter. However, his goals were not enough as Forest held unto their lead after Morgan Gibss-White had extended it immediately after, bringing the game to a 3-2 full-time result. Before the Forest clash, Emegha put Chelsea ahead at home when they hosted Leeds United last week. Unfortunately, he could not save the team from capitulating to a 1-4 defeat in the game. But beyond his growing reputation in England, Emegha has an interesting connection to Nigeria. Born in The Hague, Netherlands, to a Togolese father and a Nigerian mother, the powerful forward has West African roots. His Nigerian heritage makes him a player of interest to Nigerian football fans, particularly those following the growing number of players of Nigerian descent making waves in European football. However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football. His latest goals against Nottingham Forest are another early signs of what he could offer Chelsea. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. nigeria.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
nigeria.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. nigeria.title: UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom government has outlined two conditions under which travellers can bring goods into the country without paying customs duty or tax, warning that items outside the permitted categories or allowance limits could attract charges. According to the UK government’s customs guidelines, travellers can bring goods into the country tax-free under two conditions. First condition is personal use. Goods must be intended for the traveller’s own use rather than for commercial purposes or resale. Second condition is gifts. Travellers can also bring goods intended as presents for other people without paying customs duty, provided they remain within the applicable personal allowance. The rules apply to foreign visitors and British residents returning from overseas, regardless of whether the items were purchased from regular shops or duty-free outlets at airports. However, the exemptions are subject to personal allowance limits, which determine the quantity and value of goods travellers can bring into the country without incurring additional charges. The applicable allowance depends on where a traveller is arriving from and whether the destination is Great Britain, comprising England, Scotland and Wales, or Northern Ireland. The government also warned that goods intended for business or resale do not qualify for personal allowances. Such items must be declared to customs regardless of their value or quantity. Travellers are also required to declare goods that exceed their personal allowances or fall under banned and restricted categories before crossing the border. Declarations can be made online up to five days, or 120 hours, before arrival in the UK. The authorities warned that failure to comply with customs regulations could result in the seizure of goods and, in some cases, the vehicle used to transport them. Offenders may also face financial penalties or prosecution. The post UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
nigeria.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

The Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, disclosed this in a video shared on his X handle on Friday, saying Nigeria had already communicated its interest to the Confederation of African Football (CAF). A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Kyle Shanahan Rules Brock Purdy Out For Seahawks Clash
sports.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images An ankle injury will cause San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy to miss Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan on Friday. Mac Jones takes over as the starter, with Kurtis Rourke serving as the backup, according to ESPN reporter Nick Wagoner. The team made this call after Purdy did not practice all week and his injury did not heal fast enough to allow him to suit up. During the second quarter of last week’s victory over the Minnesota Vikings, Purdy injured his left ankle. The injury happened when Purdy tried to escape defensive lineman Jalen Redmond and his foot bent awkwardly as he went to the ground. Shanahan knew about the issue at halftime but said it did not change how he called plays for the rest of that game. The coach ruled the injury out on Friday because it simply did not improve during the week. A Mid-Level Ankle Issue Shanahan explained the specific nature of the injury while speaking to reporters on Friday. “Anytime it’s not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse,” Shanahan said. He noted that the team had a feeling by Wednesday that Purdy would not be ready. “Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. [It] didn’t heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down,” the coach added. Purdy does not require surgery, and the expectation is that he will be ready for Week 13 versus the New York Giants. Shanahan remains optimistic about the timeline for his recovery. “It’s too soon [to tell] but I’m pretty optimistic about it,” Shanahan said. He acknowledged the sudden change in plans but expressed hope for the future. “But I was about this week to start and then it changes. So, hopefully it’ll be all right,” he told the press. Mac Jones Steps Up Again Jones is no stranger to this situation for the 49ers. In 2025, when Purdy suffered a turf toe injury, he started eight games in Purdy’s stead. During those contests, the 49ers went 5-3 with Jones posting a 62.7 QBR. He threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions in that span. This season, Jones has seen action only in mop-up duty, where he completed one pass on one attempt for 5 yards. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Left tackle Trent Williams voiced strong support for Jones after seeing his preparation this week. Williams highlighted the team’s confidence in him based on his past performance. “He was great last year when we needed him,” Williams said. The team expects Jones to handle the pressure of this big divisional game. “We expect him to be good this year,” Williams added. Shanahan praised Jones for his work during the week leading up to the matchup. “Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this with him last year, so everyone’s got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp, and he’s the same guy every day. It’s been a good week with Mac,” per ProFoo

sports.description: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks passes the ball while being pressured by Romello Height #94 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter at Lumen Field on Oct. 11, 2026 in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) When the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Seattle to play the Seahawks seven weeks ago, it represented a big moment for both teams. The 49ers won, remaining undefeated, and have gone 4-1 since. After narrowly losing, the Seahawks have stumbled to 3-2. With Kyle Shanahan 's club riding high and leading the NFC but facing a game with Brock Purdy on the sidelines, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to these key questions going into Sunday's rematch. First, a general NFL question: the drama in Pittsburgh. Have we seen the last of Aaron Rodgers in uniform? Harrison Rich: It's often hard to side with Aaron Rodgers, but he seems to have the stronger argument here over Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. ESPN confirmed Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy , including sleeping in quarterback meetings and breaking down a halftime huddle by saying "1-2-3 Packers." Rodgers was waived Wednesday, but I'd imagine he plays football again in 2026 - assuming he wants to. He was still playing at a fairly high level and led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record before his ousting. Eric Branch: The constant in Aaron Rodgers' family and work drama: Aaron Rodgers. Given the late-career strife he's often been responsible for causing, it's notable that Rodgers' 22-season career began with him spending three good-soldier seasons sitting behind Brett Favre. Rodgers took a flamethrower to his long relationship with Mike McCarthy. It sounds as if much of what he alleged is true, but he broke an NFL code and left his playoff-contending teammates to deal with the fallout. Has he played his last snap? Not if an injury to a starting QB creates an urgent need. As former Cardinals GM Steve Keim once said of NFL teams rationalizing character concerns: "If Hannibal Lecter ran a 4.3, we'd probably diagnose it as an eating disorder." Ann Killion: I wouldn't be shocked if some playoff-bound team suffers an injury at quarterback and brings Rodgers in. I mean, who would be better? But, as the Black Friday broadcast team pointed out, Rodgers had already said this is his last year and has also emphasized that when he was done playing he will pull a "Keyser Soze" and disappear from public view. (Interesting to hear fellow former Cal Bear Tony Gonzalez put Rodgers on blast.) Yet there he was, airing his dirty laundry on the Pat McAfee show, blowtorching the coach he won a Super Bowl with, and texting Al Michaels during the Friday broadcast to further litigate his case. The guy desperately needs the spotlight. Pittsburgh crushed Denver, sending the message that they don't need Rodgers (though the players all still seem to like him). Rodgers' most amazing feat? Turning hapless McCarthy into a sympathetic character. Fred Warner

sports.description: Stuart McCloskey featured in all 12 Ireland Tests this year while Ulster team-mate James McNabney marked his second cap with two tries off the bench [Getty Images] Ireland's return to Twickenham may not have produced more viral moments like Stuart McCloskey barrelling Marcus Smith into touch, but it did yield the victory needed to close the book on what head coach Andy Farrell considers a successful year. Farrell has not shied away from his intention to use the November window as a World Cup test run: four weekends, four games, heavy-hitting opposition, six-day turnarounds. Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off at a half-empty Allianz Stadium, however, felt like a comedown in the wake of a nail-biting win over world champions South Africa. But winning ugly is an important feature for the best teams and carving out a gritty 38-14 success over Australia is a reflection of the progress Farrell has been demanding to see. Casting his eye over the campaign as a whole, he sounded upbeat as he spoke about a noticeable uptick in his squad's desire to grow with the World Cup coming into view. "We've certainly seen a shift in our appetite to want to grow and get better," said Farrell. "That's been very evident in the camp. It transfers sometimes to games, sometimes it doesn't, but we've seen the step up as far as that's concerned. "It's been a very successful campaign for that alone, but we've got to keep that going now and taking big steps forward." Replicating the punchy, spirited display that brought down South Africa in Dublin last week was always going to be a big ask, and Ireland certainly showed signs of weariness during a clunky first-half display that a more accurate team than Australia would have punished. sports.title: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship
sports.description: DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West played for its sixth PIAA District One football championship on Friday night. The Bucks won District One onfield titles under Mike Pettine in 1993 and 1997-99, as well as Mike Carey in 2000. Spring-Ford, like CB West, went into the game at War Memorial Field with identical 12-1 records. The Bucks finished the job, downing the Rams 34-0 behind a dominant rushing attack and suffocating defense. Senior Lou Cipollo ran for a pair of touchdowns while seniors Nick Miletto and Braylen Cope both scored a rushing touchdown. CB West will face the St. Joseph Prep/Nazareth winner in next weekend’s Class 6A semifinals. Prep led Nazareth 49-20 at the start of the fourth quarter. West had reached the district title game in 2022, when it lost at Garnet Valley, while Spring-Ford fell to Coatesville for the 2012 district championship. This is the Bucks' first district title in 26 seasons. Rob Rowan’s CB West squad defeated Perkiomen Valley 56-42, Central Bucks East 44-21 and Council Rock South 30-13 to reach the final, while Spring-Ford topped Quakertown 42-28, Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 and top-seeded Downingtown East 17-14 at districts. *Check back later tonight for much more on the game. What’s next for Spring-Ford Football? The season ended for the Rams. What’s next for Central Bucks West Football? The Bucks will face St. Joseph Prep or Nazareth in the state semifinals next weekend. sports.title: Mangiapane Scores Twice, Blackhawks Beat Rangers For Fourth Straight Win
sports.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but it was enough to defeat the New York Rangers (13-11-1) 2-1 at the United Center on Friday. Andrew Mangiapane scored both of Chicago’s goals, his first two tallies of the season, Oliver Moore had two assists, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 31 shots as the Blackhawks extended their winning streak to four games. The Blackhawks are now 6-1-1 in eight games since an abysmal 0-3 Southeastern road trip earlier this month. Mika Zibanejad scored for the Rangers, while Dylan Garand started in net and allowed two goals on 10 shots faced. Adam Fox extended his point streak to five games with an assist on Zibanejad’s power-play goal. All three goals in Friday’s game were power-play tallies, with the Blackhawks converting on both opportunities and extending their goal streak to eight games. Since opening the season with a 5-for-51 stretch, the power play has now scored on 13 of its last 22 opportunities. Even without Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi , the man advantage continued its red-hot stretch, and it was the second unit stepping up to score both goals against the Rangers. Entering Friday, New York had the NHL’s top-ranked penalty kill and had allowed a league-low three power-play goals in their first 12 road games. But even without their best offensive players, including captain Connor Bedard and Bowen Byram , the power play impressively still found a way to generate all the offense needed against a stout Rangers’ PK for a fourth straight win. Defensively, Knight was outstanding for the second straight game, as the 25-year-old was credited with 2.03 goals saved above expected against the Rangers. Over his last three outings — all wins — Knight has stopped 92 of 97 shots for a .948 save percentage. While the Rangers outshot and outchanced the Blackhawks by a wide margin, they were credited with only 10 high-danger scoring chances at even strength. Much like Wednesday’s win in Seattle, the Hawks’ defense didn’t allow many threatening looks. The defensemen and forwards also selflessly stepped in the shooting lane, recording 22 blocked shots in Friday’s win. technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources.
